subject: Understanding Confirmatory Factor Aanalysis nested models with more/fewer factors

messages.author: b5ebbeae393deb7d
messages.subject: Understanding Confirmatory Factor Aanalysis nested models with more/fewer factors
parts:
Hello all,

In this post (and reply) it is suggested that you can use anova() to compare a model with more factors against one with less.  To be specific, the models I'm considering look like...

Model 1 (7 factor)
f1 =~ v1 + v2 + v3  + v4 + v5
f2 =~ v6 + v7
f3 =~ v8 + v9 + v10 + v11
f4 =~ v12 + v13 + v14
f5 =~ v15 + v16
f6 =~ v17 + v18
f7 =~ v19 + v20


Model 2 (6 factor - same as above with f5 and f7 as same factor)
f1 =~ v1 + v2 + v3  + v4 + v5
f2 =~ v6 + v7
f3 =~ v8 + v9 + v10 + v11
f4 =~ v12 + v13 + v14
f5 =~ v15 + v16 + v19 + v20
f6 =~ v17 + v18

I can run these two models in lavaan and anova() gives me 

Scaled Chi Square Difference Test (method = "satorra.bentler.2001")

           Df   AIC   BIC  Chisq Chisq diff Df diff Pr(>Chisq)
Model 1   149 17159 17467 373.80                              
Model 2   155 17150 17436 377.65     2.8341       6     0.8294

If I try to manually create the nesting, by adding a constraint to the first model such that the correlation between f5 and f7 = 1, (as also suggested by this post on Stack Exchange) I get...

Model 2b (7 factor reduced to 6 by constraint, so clearly nested)
f1 =~ v1 + v2 + v3  + v4 + v5
f2 =~ v6 + v7
f3 =~ v8 + v9 + v10 + v11
f4 =~ v12 + v13 + v14
f5 =~ v15 + v16
f6 =~ v17 + v18
f7 =~ v19 + v20
f5 ~~ 1*f7

Scaled Chi Square Difference Test (method = "satorra.bentler.2001")

          Df   AIC   BIC  Chisq Chisq diff Df diff Pr(>Chisq)
Model 1  149 17159 17467 373.80                              
Model 2b 150 17157 17462 373.83   0.022915       1     0.8797


along with a warning about non-positive definiteness in the correlation matrix of latent variables when I run Model 2b.

Intuitively, the second approach seems correct to me.  There is only one parameter constraint difference between the 7-factor and 6-factor models.  However, the published literature I've seen that compares these models always reports a Df.diff of 6 for the comparison.  Where are the other df coming from (assuming they are correct, which the lavaan result would suggest is the case)

Wild guess - does it have something to do with the equality of correlations between the other factors and both f5 and f7?

Thanks for any insight you can offer.

regards

James

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Understanding Confirmatory Factor Aanalysis nested models with more/fewer factors
parts: Wild guess - does it have something to do with the equality of correlations between the other factors and both f5 and f7?

Yes, that's exactly it.  If those are the same variable, that implies their relationships with any other variable (e.g., with f1, with f2, etc.) would be identical.  Also, fixing the covariance to 1 only implies their correlation is 1 if the factors are standardized to have variances == 1.  You can do this with the argument std.lv = TRUE
